questions.question: Every refund run ends with 'Done, I've refunded your order.' Why isn't an answer-only eval enough?
options: The answer can be identical while the actions differ: wrong order, wrong amount, loops
questions.explanation: What the agent did lives in the trajectory, especially for side effects.

questions.question: The over-refund run ($790 on a $79 order) has edit distance 0 to the reference. Why?
options: It compares tool names only; the run used the same tools in the same order with a wrong argument
questions.explanation: Name-based metrics can't see arguments. Argument-aware matchers can.

questions.question: The 'different but fine' run checks the policy before looking up the order. Which metrics fail it?
options: Exact match and in-order, though the run is correct
questions.explanation: Strict reference matching punishes valid alternative paths.

questions.question: When does the rule 'lookup_order before issue_refund' fire?
options: Only if issue_refund happens and no lookup_order came before it
questions.explanation: Ordering rules constrain the side effect; whether a refund was required is a separate rule.

questions.question: Where should ordering constraints go in a trajectory spec?
options: Only around side effects and dependencies that matter (e.g. look up before refunding)
questions.explanation: Constraining everything recreates exact match and its false failures.

questions.question: An agent calls lookup_order with the same arguments four times after timeouts. Which signals catch it?
options: Low precision and the repeated-identical-call rule
questions.explanation: Recall stays 1.0 because the needed call happened; loops show up as extra calls and repeats.
